Mesoproterozoic (ca. 1.26 Ga) Srednecheremshansk mafic–ultramafic
intrusion in the southern Siberia: Signature of the Mackenzie event
in Siberia
D.P. Gladkochuba,*, T.V. Donskayaa, S.A. Pisarevskyb, A.B. Kotovc, E.B. Salnikovac,
A.S. Mekhonoshind, E.V. Sklyarova, E.I. Demonterovaa, A.M. Mazukabzova, A.V. Stepanovae,
K.M. Konstantinova,f

bEarth Dynamics Research Group, The Institute for Geoscience Research (TIGeR), School of Earth and Planetary Sciences, Curtin University, WA 6845, Australia
cInstitute of Precambrian Geology and Geochronology of the Russian Academy of Sciences, St. Petersburg 199034, Russia
dA.P. Vinogradov Institute of Geochemistry, Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Irkutsk 664033, Russia

A R T I C L E I N F O A B S T R A C T
Keywords: Several published Mesoproterozoic paleogeographic reconstructions suggest proximity of northern Laurentia and
U-Pb baddeleyite age southern Siberia. However, the apparent absence of the traces of the ca. 1.27 Ga giant Mackenzie magmatic event
Geochemistry in southern Siberia was somewhat contradictory to this hypothesis. Here we present geochronological, miner-
Paleomagnetism
alogical, geochemical, Nd isotopic, and paleomagnetic data from the Srednecheremshansk dyke-shaped intru-
Mackenzie magmatic event
sion, which was recently found in the Sharyzhalgay uplift of the southern part of the Siberian craton and which
Mesoproterozoic
can be related to the Mackenzie event. The plagioclase-bearing peridotite of this intrusion yielded U-Pb (ID-
Siberian craton
TIMS) baddeleyite concordia age of 1260 ±3 Ma, which is interpreted as the time of their emplacement. This age
is close to the previously published baddeleyite age of gabbro from the same intrusion (1258 ±5 Ma). The
Srednecheremshansk intrusion is composed of ultramafic and mafic rocks. The main rock-forming minerals of the
intrusion are olivine, orthopyroxene, clinopyroxene, phlogopite, and plagioclase in various proportions. Sulfide
mineralization of the intrusion is represented by pentlandite nodules. The chemical composition of Sredne-
cheremshansk ultramafic and mafic rocks correspond to subalkaline peridotite gabbro and gabbro. These rocks
are characterized by negative εNd(t) values range from (cid:0) 6.3 to (cid:0) 6.9. Ultramafic and mafic rocks have similar
geochemical and isotopic characteristics, indicating their generation from a single subcontinental lithospheric
mantle source. The chemical composition of the Srednecheremshansk intrusion is similar to those of the ca. 1.27
Ga Muskox mafic–ultramafic intrusion of the Mackenzie Large Igneous Province in northern Laurentia. Paleo-
magnetic data permit a variety of possible Laurentia-Siberia reconstructions in Mesoproterozoic. The combina-
tion of geochronological, geochemical, and paleomagnetic data allows the relation of the Srednecheremshansk
intrusion with the Mackenzie magmatic event.

2. Geological setting and petrography
The Srednecheremshansk intrusion is located in the Irkut block of the
Sharyzhalgay uplift within the Tungus superterrane of the southern part
of the Siberian craton (Fig. 1a, b). The Sharyzhalgay uplift comprises
two granite-greenstone (Onot and Bulun) and two granulite-gneiss
(Irkut and Kitoy) blocks (Fig. 1b) (Grabkin and Melnikov, 1980).
Blocks are mainly composed of Archean rocks and intruded by Paleo-
proterozoic post-collisional granitoids (Fig. 1b) (Donskaya and Glad-
kochub, 2021). The final assembly of all blocks probably took place in
Paleoproterozoic, simultaneously with the formation of the Siberian
craton (Donskaya, 2020).
The Srednecheremshansk intrusion cuts Archean biotite and garnet-
biotite gneisses of the Cheremshansk Fm. of the Irkut block of the
Sharyzhalgay uplift (Fig. 1b, 2). It is NNE-trending and dips 75–80◦ to
the west (Ernst et al., 2016; Mekhonoshin et al., 2016). The intrusion is
dyke-shaped (Fig. 2a). It can be traced for 6 km and has thickness of
100–200 m (Mekhonoshin et al., 2016). The intrusion is composed of
gabbro, olivine gabbro, gabbronorite, olivine gabbronorite, plagioclase-
bearing peridotite (Fig. 2b) (Mekhonoshin et al., 2016). There are mafic
units in the margins and an ultramafic unit in the interior of the intru-
sion (Fig. 2b). Ore mineralization of the intrusion is represented by
pyrrhotite-pentlandite nodules within the ore zone 0.5 m thick
(Mekhonoshin et al., 2016). U-Pb baddeleyite age of the Srednecher-
emshansk gabbro is 1258 ±5 Ma (Ernst et al., 2016; Mekhonoshin et al.,
2016).
Rock-forming minerals of the Srednecheremshansk intrusion are
olivine, orthopyroxene, clinopyroxene, phlogopite, and plagioclase in
various proportions (Fig. 3). Ilmenite, Cr-spinel, apatite, baddeleyite,
zirconolite, and monazite are accessory minerals. Ore minerals are
Fig. 2. Schematic geological map of the Srednecheremshansk intrusion area
pentlandite, heazlewoodite, smithite, chalcopyrite, chalcocite, covellite,
with sample localities (a); a section along the borehole 9 (b).
bornite, native copper, wurtzite, and sphalerite. Secondary minerals are
represented by serpentine, chlorite, magnetite, and rutile.
Pisarevsky et al., 2014, 2021; Cawood et al., 2020; Gladkochub et al.,
2021). The second option suggests a relative movement between Siberia

4.4. Paleomagnetism
The Srednecheremshansk rocks are characterized by low initial ra-
tios of 143Nd/144Nd, varying from 0.511829 to 0.511892, as well as
negative εNd(t) values range from (cid:0) 6.3 to (cid:0) 6.9 (Table 2). During the paleomagnetic sampling we tried to avoid places with
visible ore occurrences. The intensity of the natural remanent magne-
tization (NRM) is mainly between 500 mA/m and 10 A/m. However,

5. Discussion
5.1. Age and petrogenesis of Srednecheremshansk ultramafic and mafic
rocks
Our new U-Pb baddeleyite concordia age of Srednecheremshansk
plagioclase-bearing peridotite (1260 ±3 Ma) matches the baddeleyite
age of gabbro from this intrusion (1258 ± 5 Ma) (Ernst et al., 2016;
Mekhonoshin et al., 2016). The close age and similar geochemical
characteristics of the Srednecheremshansk ultramafic and mafic rocks
(Figs. 6, 7) indicate that all rocks in the intrusion were produced from a
single parental melt.
The studied Srednecheremshansk ultramafic and mafic rocks
demonstrate negative Nb-Ta and Ta anomalies in primitive mantle-
normalized variation diagrams (Fig. 7b) and strongly negative εNd(t)
values varying from (cid:0) 6.3 to (cid:0) 6.9 (Table 2). The Srednecheremshansk
rocks fall above MORB-OIB array in the Th/Yb – Nb/Yb diagram of
Pearce (2008), suggesting subduction or crustal component’s involve-
ment in their source (Fig. 11a). The studied ultramafic and mafic rocks
are characterized by similarity in REE and multielement spectra (Fig. 7
a–b), similar ratios of strongly incompatible elements, including Th/Yb,
Nb/Yb, Th/Nb, Th/Ta, Zr/Nb (Fig. 11 a–d), which reflect their origin
Fig. 10. Stereoplots of the sample mean paleomagnetic directions of the
from a homogeneous mantle source. The Srednecheremshansk rocks are

(Fig. 11 b–d). Strongly negative εNd(t) values but a narrow εNd(t) range
